newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil eases as Iraqi sales loom nearer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil eases as Iraqi sales loom nearer.

text.p: World oil prices drifted lower on Friday as downward pressure from looming Iraqi oil sales was partially offset by strong cargo markets for crude oil and gasoline.
Brent crude oil, the world benchmark grade, was down eight cents at $18.61 a barrel at 1440 GMT.
Oil prices have fallen 25 percent this year but are well clear of $17.32 a 13-month low hit over a month ago.

Iraq is expected to more than double its oil exports next month to around 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) to make up for a gap between the end of the first "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations and the beginning of the second.

The second deal began on June 8 but Iraq has delayed exporting oil for two months and will now have to sell it at a much higher rate in August than previously reckoned or forego some of its sales under the scheme.
India said it would try to buy up to 7.3 million barrels of Iraqi crude when the deal gets underway.
Despite the potential downward pressure from Iraqi oil sales the underlying oil market was well supported amid steady demand for refined oil products and a surging market for Brent cargoes.
Gasoline stocks in the United States fell sharply and there has also been scattered demand for other oil products in Europe and Asia and several supply scares in recent days.
In the North Sea the Nelson oilfield, which feeds into the Forties crude oil system, has had to cut output by 60,000 bpd due to technical problems.
Meanwhile, hurricane Danny in the Gulf of Mexico delayed at least one tanker from deliverying crude oil into the United States and caused a refinery run by Chevron Corp to shut.
